insights.insight: 10,915 cryptographically verified receipts represent confirmed purchase events — not modeled intent. At $908K cumulative GMV, each receipt carries an average basket of ~$83, making this a high-value, post-transaction signal set that probabilistic targeting cannot replicate.

At a 14-day run rate of $366,559 — 40% of all-time volume compressed into two weeks — the network crosses $1M GMV before April 16. The pace is structurally intact; the 7-day dip from $248K to $190K is a window-roll artifact, not a demand signal.

The April 12 heartbeat recorded 22 simultaneously active CBSAs — a network record — including first entries from WI, NC, and RI non-metro areas. For brands whose customers over-index in secondary and rural markets, this is a rare verified-purchase signal outside the usual coastal concentration.

insights.topic: Velocity pattern: higher highs on each recovery
insights.insight: Token velocity has set successive records — 1.008x, then 1.232x, now 1.241x — with each post-dip recovery exceeding the prior peak. Acceleration holding above 1.0x throughout confirms the oscillation is geographic expansion rhythm, not demand decay.

SaaS subscriptions entered the receipt network for the first time on April 9, alongside warehouse/bulk retail (Costco) on April 11. For CMOs planning cross-category attribution, the signal set is no longer limited to grocery or CPG — the addressable data footprint is widening.

insights.topic: Single-cycle GMV concentration risk and opportunity
insights.insight: The April 9 burst added $56K GMV in four hours on only 42 receipts — an average ticket above $1,300 per receipt. This signals a high-AOV buyer cohort exists within the network, relevant for luxury, B2B, and big-ticket brands evaluating verified-purchase audience targeting.
